paite: Huchihlaiin Elipha Teman miin a dawnga, hichiin a chi hi:
english: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

paite: Min nang honhoulim pih tum leh na zadah diam? Hizongleh pau louin kua a om thei dia?
english: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

paite: Ngaiin, mi tampi na hilhtaa, huan khut hatloute na hihhatta hi.
english: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.

paite: A puklai mah na thuten a dingsaka, khuk hatloute na kipsak hi.
english: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.

paite: Himahleh tuin na tungah a hongtunga, na baha; nang a honkhoiha, na buaita.
english: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

paite: Pathian an kihtakna na muanna hi lou hia, na lametna na lampite muanhuaina?
english: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?

paite: Theigigein, ka honngen hi, hoih hina pia, mangthang ngei kua ahia? ahihkeileh koilaiah ahia midik satkhiaka om?
english: “Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

paite: Kei muh danin, thulimlouhna leilette ahi ua, buaina tuha, huaimah atte.
english: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.

paite: Pathian huin a mangthang ua, huan a hehna mutin himanin a om uhi.
english: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.

paite: Humpinelkai huham leh, humpinelkai hangsan aw leh, humpinelkai tuailai hate, a kitan ta.
english: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

paite: Samat taksap jiakin humpinelkai tek a mangthanga, huan humpinelkai noute a dalhjak ua.
english: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.

paite: Tuin a gukin thil ka kiang a hongtunga, ka bilin huaia huauna a sangta hi.
english: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.

paite: Jan mengmuhna akipana ngaihtuahnate ah, mite nakpi taka a ihmut san lai un,
english: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

paite: Launa ka tungah a hontunga, linna, huaiin ka guhte tengteng a singa.
english: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

paite: Huailaiin ka mai maah kha a paia; ka chimul a ding ta hi.
english: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.

paite: Ka ding kinkena, himahleh huaia a kilatdan ka theikak theita keia; a lim tuh ka mit maah a oma; daihna a oma, huan aw ka jaa,
english: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,

paite: Pathian sangin sithei mihing a dik zo ding hia? A Bawlpa sangin mihing siangthou zo ding hia? chiin.
english: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

paite: Ngaiin, a sikhate ah muanna akoih keia; huan a angelte haiin a ngoh hi:
english: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.

paite: Tungman ina teng amaute hi diak na un chia, a suangphum leivuia oma, leikha maa chimsia:
english: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!

paite: Jingsang leh nitak kikalin hihsiatin a om ua: theihlouh hialin khantawnin a mangthang uhi.Amau sunga a puanin-khau uh bohkhiak touh hi lou hia? a si ua, huan pilna tel louin.
english: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.

paite: Amau sunga a puanin-khau uh bohkhiak touh hi lou hia? a si ua, huan pilna tel louin.
english: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’
